analysis.evidence: לֶמֶךְ (Lamech) is the subject, שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים (two wives) is the object, and לוֹ (for himself) refers back to Lamech. Together they express that Lamech took two wives for himself.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לֶמֶךְ. Its derivation is unknown.
draft.definition: Lamech, the man identified in Genesis 4:19 as the husband of Adah and Zillah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:19 names Lamech as the man who took two wives and then identifies each wife by name.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקַּח לוֹ לֶמֶךְ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים, לֶמֶךְ names the subject of וַיִּקַּח, “he took.” The rest of the verse names his two wives, Adah and Zillah. The verse gives no derivation for his name.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of the man who took Adah and Zillah as wives.

analysis.evidence: שְׁתֵּי counts נָשִׁים in the phrase “two wives.” The verse then names one wife עָדָה and the second צִלָּה.
In וַיִּקַּח לוֹ לֶמֶךְ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים, Lamech takes two wives for himself. The verse names one Adah and the other Zillah.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Correct the existing Genesis 10:25 evidence note for identifying-name at word index 0. Joktan is the name of Peleg’s brother.
draft.definition: A name by which a person or other bearer is identified.
draft.evidence: In וְשֵׁם אָחִיו יָקְטָן, אָחִיו refers to Peleg’s brother and יָקְטָן supplies that brother’s name.

analysis.evidence: In שֵׁם הָאַחַת עָדָה, שֵׁם הָאַחַת means “the name of the one,” and עָדָה gives that wife’s name, Adah.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state before הָאַחַת, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After introducing שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים (“two wives”), the verse pairs שֵׁם הָאַחַת עָדָה (“the name of the one was Adah”) with וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית צִלָּה (“and the name of the second was Zillah”).
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to אַחַת, a feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral referring to one of the two wives.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Adah linked to the root article ad.
draft.definition: Adah is a Hebrew female personal name. In Genesis 4:19 it names one of Lamech’s wives.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:19 identifies Adah by the naming formula שֵׁם הָאַחַת עָדָה. Isaiah 61:10 uses the verb עדה of a bride adorning herself with jewels, suggesting a possible derivation for the name.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם הָאַחַת עָדָה means “the name of the one was Adah.” The parallel וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית צִלָּה gives Zillah as the name of the second wife.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Adah, one of Lamech’s two wives

analysis.evidence: The verse names Lamech’s two wives in sequence. שֵׁם הָאַחַת עָדָה names Adah as the first, and וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית צִלָּה names Zillah as the second.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute ordinal adjective used substantivally.

analysis.evidence: The parallel clauses שֵׁם הָאַחַת עָדָה and וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית צִלָּה name the two wives in turn. The first is Adah and the second is Zillah.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular personal name, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the second of Lamech’s two wives.
